chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Redman's road band and his feel for dance tempos
summary: After Connie's Inn the band went on the road; Redman understood dance tempos, which also made McKinney's a great dance band.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Oh, yes, CBS, coast to coast. And we stayed in Connie's Inn until the fall, about, well, I'll say December and then we went on the road with that band. And fantastic that band was, it was so beautiful every place we went. And it was a band that you could dance to. Don knew the value of dance tempos, you see, whether it was a waltz, whether it was a fox trot in those days.
You know, going back to McKinney's band, you know, that's what made McKinney's band such a great dance band was Don Redman, --

-- you see? Because he believed in playing music that people could dance to, and you'd always see the people just skim around the floor beautifully, you know, and relaxed because it was that type of band, that type of music.
